variable.name: average air temperature
variable.source: NASA POWER (MERRA-2), monthly, 0.5 x 0.625 degree grid

trend.method: Sen's slope; Mann-Kendall test with variance scaled by lag 1 autocorrelation of what is left after a smooth curve (effective sample size; a straight line for ranges under 20 years); Benjamini-Hochberg FDR on maps

sentence: Since 2001, average air temperature here rose by 0.70 °C in total (95% range 0.08 to 1.23), a rate of 0.29 °C per decade. Moderate evidence that this is a real change: with nothing really changing, a trend this strong would appear by luck only 2.7% of the time.
